newsitem.title: USA: Ingersoll-Rand says new orders increase.
newsitem.headline: Ingersoll-Rand says new orders increase.

text.p: Ingersoll-Rand, the industrial equipment and components maker, said Wednesday that new orders increased in the second quarter and it believes it is on target to turn in a record performance for the year.
The company said new orders rose eight percent to $1.8 billion in the second quarter with much of the improvement seen in the U.S. markets.

Commenting on the improvement, James Perrella, I-R's chairman, president and chief executive officer said, "We continue to expect a record performance for the full year, and we have set a target to achieve 12-15 percent compounded earnings growth over the next four years, before major acquisitions."
I-R showed improvement in its standard machinery as well as its bearings, locks and tools division.
The company said in a statement that standard machinery sales rose 4.5 percent to $834.5 million reflecting strength in the U.S. markets for construction and general industry.
In its bearings, locks and tools division sales increased 25 percent to 781.7 million.
However, the company reported a decline in sales in its engineered equipment division. The division, which is now

soley made up of the Ingersoll-Dresser Pump Company were $221.2 million. That was a drop from the same time last year of 34 percent. However, the company explained that the Ingersoll-Dresser Pump Company's interest charge totaled $7.1 million, versus $4.2 million in the second quarter of last year. This item represents the portion of IDP's earnings allocable to I-R's joint venture partner, Dresser Industries Inc, which holds a minority interest in IDP. I-R said 1997 second quarter results indicate that IDP's earnings were higher than the amount reported in the second quarter of last year.
The company said the sale of its Clark-Hurth business, effective Feb 14, leaves the equipment division solely composed of the Ingersoll-Dresser Pump Co.
